indicators.name: Airspace violations above the 90-day baseline
indicators.description: Monthly count of Russian drones, missiles or aircraft violating NATO, EU or Moldovan airspace, compared with the 90-day baseline in the incident database.
indicators.last_evidence: Five airspace incidents in 30 days against a 90-day baseline of 1.3 a month.

indicators.name: Russian drone and missile tracks near the Polish, Romanian and Moldovan borders
indicators.description: Russian strike routes passing close to the Polish, Romanian and Moldovan borders, the usual source of stray drones and missiles.
indicators.last_evidence: Russian drone routes to Volyn and Lviv pass within a few kilometres of the Polish border.

indicators.name: GPS interference over the Baltic and Finland
indicators.description: GPS jamming or spoofing over the Baltic Sea, the Baltic states and Finland that disrupts aviation or shipping or draws official statements.
indicators.last_evidence: Jamming forced two Helsinki–Tallinn diversions on 11 October.

indicators.name: Sabotage incidents and arrests above baseline
indicators.description: Sabotage incidents and arrests for sabotage plots linked to Russia, compared with the 90-day baseline.

indicators.name: Undersea cable and pipeline incidents
indicators.description: Damage to undersea cables or pipelines in European waters, and related detentions of vessels.
indicators.last_evidence: Gulf of Finland data cable damaged on 16 October.

indicators.name: Airport or port closures caused by drones
indicators.description: Closures of airports, ports or military bases caused by drone overflights that officials link to a state actor.

indicators.name: Russian units redeploying toward Finland, the Baltics, Kaliningrad or Belarus
indicators.description: Russian units moving toward the Leningrad and Moscow military districts, Kaliningrad or Belarus, or new formations standing up near Finland and the Baltic states.

indicators.name: Mobilisation or large reserve call-ups
indicators.description: A new Russian mobilisation wave or reserve call-ups well above routine conscription.

indicators.name: Exercises larger than declared, or snap readiness checks near NATO borders
indicators.description: Russian or Belarusian exercises that exceed their declared size, or snap readiness checks close to NATO borders.

indicators.name: Ammunition, fuel or medical stockpiling near NATO borders
indicators.description: Build-up of ammunition, fuel or medical supplies near NATO borders beyond what the war in Ukraine explains.

indicators.name: Nuclear readiness changes, or nuclear deployments to Belarus or Kaliningrad
indicators.description: Changes in Russian nuclear readiness, or nuclear or Oreshnik deployments in Belarus or Kaliningrad.

indicators.name: Russian pretext narratives about the Baltics, Narva, Kaliningrad or Suwałki
indicators.description: Official Russian narratives that could build a pretext for action against a NATO state: "compatriots" in the Baltics, Narva, Kaliningrad transit, the Suwałki corridor.

indicators.name: Diplomatic warning signs: embassy drawdowns, families leaving, airspace closures
indicators.description: Russian diplomats' families leaving European capitals, embassy drawdowns, or unusual airspace closures.

indicators.name: Public disclosures of cyber footholds in European grids, rail or telecoms
indicators.description: Official disclosures that Russian actors hold access inside European power grids, rail or telecoms networks.

indicators.name: Changes in US force posture or commitment in Europe (amplifier)
indicators.description: Announced or observed changes in US forces in Europe or in the US commitment to Article 5; an amplifier of other risks.

indicators.name: A NATO Article 4 consultation requested
indicators.description: An ally requests consultations under Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty.

indicators.name: NATO Article 5 invoked
indicators.description: An ally invokes collective defence under Article 5.

indicators.name: A US decision on Tomahawk-class long-range weapons for Ukraine
indicators.description: A US decision to supply, or to refuse, Tomahawk-class long-range strike weapons to Ukraine.

indicators.name: A ceasefire framework signed, or direct Putin–Zelensky talks
indicators.description: A signed ceasefire framework, or direct talks between Presidents Putin and Zelensky.

indicators.name: Russian refinery capacity offline above 20%
indicators.description: Estimates from credible reporting that more than 20% of Russian refining capacity is offline.

indicators.name: A Russian gasoline export ban or domestic fuel rationing
indicators.description: A Russian ban on gasoline or diesel exports, or rationing of fuel inside Russia.

assumptions.text: Russia avoids deliberate, attributable armed attacks on NATO territory while its main force is committed in Ukraine.
The United States remains committed to defending NATO allies under Article 5.
Most airspace incidents are spillover from strikes on Ukraine or deliberate probes below the threshold of attack, not preparation for an invasion.
Russia's covert campaign in Europe (sabotage, cables, jamming) continues regardless of battlefield or diplomatic developments.
A ceasefire in Ukraine would lower near-term incident risk but raise medium-term risk as Russian forces reconstitute near NATO borders.

medium_term.question: Will Russia conduct a deliberate, attributable armed attack on NATO territory in the next 12 months?

long_term.question: Will Russia and a NATO member be in direct armed conflict by the end of 2030?
